executive_summary: Saturday April 11, 2026 — Markets closed for the weekend. The week that was: a fragile US-Iran ceasefire brokered by Pakistan on April 7-8 unleashed a historic risk rally (Dow +1,325 pts in a single session) before reality reasserted itself Friday as March CPI printed 3.3% YoY — hottest since May 2024 — driven by a record 21.2% monthly gasoline surge, the largest since 1967. The Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed despite the truce, with only 2 tankers transiting since the ceasefire; analysts warn 6 months to restore normal traffic. AI infrastructure supercycle continues as counter-narrative: CoreWeave soared 11% Friday on a multi-year deal to power Anthropic's Claude, following a $21B Meta deal announced Thursday; NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Micron all showing extraordinary revenue momentum. Heading into the week of April 13 — first full trading week post-ceasefire — dominant catalysts are Islamabad peace negotiations (Saturday) and bank earnings season opening with JPMorgan leading. No trading decisions today — market closed (weekend).

macro_events.title: US-Iran Two-Week Ceasefire — Pakistan-Brokered Truce, Islamabad Talks Begin
macro_events.causal_chain: Feb 28: US-Israel launch 'Operation Epic Fury,' kill Supreme Leader Khamenei → 40 days of air war, Hormuz closes (100+ ships/day → near zero) → VLCC day rates hit all-time record $423K/day → Brent +$40/bbl war premium → US gasoline +40% ($1.18/gal) → March CPI 3.3% → April 7: Pakistan brokers two-week ceasefire → Dow +1,325 pts, oil -16.4% in single session → Iran demands sanctions relief + US withdrawal from Middle East bases → Trump issues new threats Friday → Islamabad negotiations begin Saturday April 11 → OUTCOME: If deal holds → oil to $70s, equity rally continues; if talks fail → oil back to $110+, inflation spiral, S&P -10%
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East (Strait of Hormuz, Iran, Israel, Lebanon, Iraq), Pakistan (mediator), Gulf states, Europe (LNG supply risk via Qatar), Asia (refinery rerouting via Cape of Good Hope)
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq/Khurais attack: Brent +15% in 24h, tanker stocks +20-35% in one week. Gulf War 1990-91: oil tripled, US recession followed. 2026 is larger in scope — a full 40-day war, not a single attack.
macro_events.counterargument: Iran agreed to ceasefire under severe military pressure and economic duress; Pakistani mediation gives both sides face-saving cover; Trump's deal-making instincts favor negotiated outcomes; oil's 12% weekly decline suggests markets assign >60% probability to sustained agreement.

macro_events.title: March CPI Surges to 3.3% — Gasoline Spike Largest Since 1967
macro_events.causal_chain: Iran war starts Feb 28 → Hormuz closes → global oil supply shock → WTI +$40/bbl → US gasoline +21.2% in March (single-month record since 1967) → gasoline accounted for 75% of March CPI monthly increase → headline CPI +0.9% MoM, +3.3% YoY (highest since May 2024) → CORE CPI +0.2% MoM, +2.6% YoY (in-line) → energy inflation risk of spreading to services via transport costs → Fed caught: cut to support growth OR hold/hike to fight inflation → 10Y yield touched 4.38% intraday before settling at 4.31% → if ceasefire holds: energy deflation reverses CPI trend by June → if ceasefire fails: 3.3% becomes floor, 4%+ in view
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US domestic (consumer prices, Fed policy), driven by Middle East energy supply; EUR also facing Dutch TTF gas pressure from Qatar LNG rerouting
macro_events.historical_analog: 1973 OPEC embargo: oil quadrupled, CPI hit 12%. 1979 Iranian Revolution: oil doubled, CPI hit 14%. 2022 Russia-Ukraine: CPI peaked at 9.1%. 2026 analog closest to 1979 — single state actor in a strategic chokepoint.
macro_events.counterargument: Core CPI at 2.6% shows underlying inflation well-contained; shelter costs hit lowest annual gain since Aug 2021 (3%); if ceasefire holds and oil retraces to $75, April CPI could print flat or negative.

macro_events.title: Strait of Hormuz Remains Effectively Closed — Recovery Could Take Six Months
macro_events.causal_chain: Feb 28 war starts → Iran closes Strait of Hormuz (21% of global oil trade, 20% of global LNG) → traffic drops 80% → IRGC charging ships $2M/tanker to transit (payable in CNY or crypto) → insurers price in war-risk → VLCC day rates hit all-time record $423K/day → Asian refiners reroute via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip) → Qatar LNG to Europe disrupted → April 7 ceasefire: only 2 tankers have transited since truce → analysts say 6 months to normalize traffic → ships await explicit safety guarantees from Iran
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Strait of Hormuz (21 miles wide) → Indian Ocean → Cape of Good Hope → Europe; Qatar LNG → Mediterranean; China/Japan/South Korea crude imports heavily impacted (60%+ transit Hormuz)
macro_events.historical_analog: 2021 Suez Canal blockage (Ever Given): 6 days, $9.6B/day of trade halted; shipping rates spiked 30-40%. Hormuz closure is orders of magnitude larger in duration and volume.
macro_events.counterargument: Saudi Aramco's East-West Pipeline (1.2M bbl/day) offers partial bypass; UAE's Habshan-Fujairah pipeline (1.5M bbl/day) provides additional relief.
